title: Reconcile sample seeding, latency sampling, and adapter modernization for evals
creator: Lian Chen
description: Background: Our end-to-end eval and load pipelines have accumulated divergent sampling strategies, fragile seeding, and multiple adapter implementations (legacy gRPC stubs, new asyncio runners, and a shim layer). This has produced non-deterministic regression results, long tail variance in latency tests, and duplicated maintenance surface across repositories. Goal: unify seeding and latency-sampling rules, standardize the adapter contract used by loadgen and eval runners, and migrate remaining legacy adapters to the async adapter interface so regression runs are reproducible and easier to maintain.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic seeding: given the same seed and corpus snapshot, regression runs produce byte-identical input streams across CI and local runs
Latency sampling parity: the sampling strategy aligns across smoke, regression, and load suites (same percentile / warmup rules documented)
Adapter conformity: all active runners use the new async adapter interface; legacy gRPC stub adapters are deprecated and disabled behind a feature flag
No regression in existing test coverage: all perf CI gates pass in runtime-1.20 branch and the nightly eval pipeline
Documentation: README for seeding/sampling rules and migration guide for adapter authors merged in docs repo
implementation_plan: Audit existing runners and adapters to inventory seeding and sampling differences (2 days)
Define canonical seeding API (seed propagation, deterministic corpus slicing) and land a compatibility shim (3 days)
Codify latency sampling policy: warmup tokens, exclusion windows, measurement percentiles; add unit tests for policy enforcement (2 days)
Refactor async adapter interface to include explicit lifecycle hooks (init, warmup, predict, close) and KV-cache contract notes (4 days)
Migrate one low-risk adapter (demo connector) to async interface and validate across CI and local reproduction (2 days)
Gradual migration: open PRs for remaining adapters, enable feature-flagged deprecation of legacy adapters, and run parallel nightly comparisons for 1 week (5 days)
Consolidate docs and add a seeding/latency cookbook in the perf-harness wiki (1 day)

2025-02-25: Latency sampling policy landed and unit-tested

2025-02-21 - Aisha Patel: Latency policy proposal reviewed; suggested tightening warmup windows for streaming scenarios. Updated unit tests to cover streaming warmups.

risks: KV-cache semantics: subtle differences in cache priming between adapters could skew warmup latency if not normalized
Release coordination: runtime-1.20 consumers may depend on legacy adapter behaviors; need feature flags to avoid surprises
Reproducibility across environments: nondeterminism from external RNGs (numpy, OS-level) may still leak into runs—requires strict RNG policy enforcement
Time: migration touches multiple repos and downstream consumers; scope creep if we try to rewrite adapters rather than adapt them
rollout_and_mitigation: Feature-flagged rollout for legacy adapter deprecation with a 2-week observation window
Nightly parallel-run dashboard to compare legacy vs migrated adapters (p50/p95/p99 + throughput + error rate)
Rollback plan: if metric divergence > 3x baseline variance, automatically re-enable legacy adapters for affected CI groups
Post-merge checklist for adapter authors: integration tests, docs, and a short performance checklist
testing_and_validation: Unit tests: deterministic seed propagation, sampling policy enforcement
Integration tests: local deterministic runs and CI smoke with fixed-corpus snapshots
Regression runs: compare weekly baselines and confirm no statistically significant regressions
Canary: enable migrated adapters for 10% of nightly runs and collect detailed traces
